To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the very early multipotent human haematopoiesis cell is negative for the PI‐linked proteins DAF and MIRL.
the DAF−, HLA‐DR−, CD34+ subset is a very early multipotent haematopoietetic stem cell population and the DAF− subset does not express the PI‐linked proteins MIRL and DAF.
a very early haematopoietecic stem cell is negative for PI‐linked proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of very early human haemopoietic progenitors.

the isolation and characterization of a very early human haemopoietic progenytor cell which is negative for HLA‐DR and positive for CD34 (MY 10) but which is negative for the PI‐linked proteins, DAF and MIRL.
the characterization of the human bone marrow stem cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the very early haematopoietically multipotential progenitor cell is a DAF‐ MIRL+ CD34+ HLA‐DR− cell.
a very early multipotent haematopoietecic progenitor cell does not express PI‐linked proteins, and that the expression of PI‐linkage is associated with a more differentiated cell.
a very early multipotent haematopoietically committed progenitor cell population exists which expresses the CD34 antigen but is negative for the expression of PI‐anchored proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PI‐linked proteins, DAF and MIRL, are expressed on the D+ subset of the bone marrow population, but are not expressed on the very early multipotental progenitor cell population.
the DAF−, MIRL− cell is a very early multipotent stem cell and that the DAF+ cell is an early committed progenitor cell.
the DAF− cell represents a very primitive multipotential haemopoietic stem cell which can be isolated from human bone marrow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PI‐linked molecules are present on early lineage‐specific progenitor cells, but not on the very early multipotent progenitor cell.
